content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, the authors mainly focus on the medical segmentation under semi- and noisy- supervision. They propose a meta-learning framework, named MLB-Seg, which could learn the adaptive weights maps to adjust the pixel-wise importance in the pseudo labels. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper is well-written and easy to follow. The authors also release the codes, which would be much helpful for this community. 

The key contributions of this work are the semi- and noisy- supervision, the adaptive weight maps, as well as the consistency-based pseudo label enhancement, only for medical segmentation tasks. One of the main concerns is the proposed framework MLB-Seg seems to be used in natural image segmentation, since there might not exist lots of differences or gaps between medical image segmentation and natural image segmentation from the manuscript. If the proposed method could work well both one the current medical segmentation as well as natural segmentation, it would be much better, and be more generous method. From this view, this work is strongly encouraged to submit to medical conference, i.e., MICCAI or vision conference, i.e., CVPR or ICCV, which prevent me vote for the acceptance. Besides, the used mean-teacher or meta-learning adaptive weights might not be sufficient novel or new for this community. 

The authors are suggested to move some adaptive weight maps from the supple to the manuscript, to support their idea.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to follow. The authors provide the codes and a detailed implementation for reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the main concerns of weakness, I vote for rejection.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The manuscript proposed a meta-learning framework, MLB-seg, for 3D medical image segmentation under semi-supervision or noisy supervision. The proposed framework introduces dynamic weight maps to reflect per-pixel importance for noisy or pseudo labels. And the weight maps are utilized in the loss computation during model training for performance improvement. The proposed framework also adopts a consistency based regularization with the “mean teacher” model to further stabilize learned weight maps. Moreover, the experimental results validate the proposed framework on two public 3D medical image segmentation datasets. Both datasets have moderate size for binary segmentation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
<Strength>

•	The paper is well-organized and well-written.

•	The experimental results supports the claims made in the manuscripts.

•	The submitted content is related to the application of deep neural networks in 3D medical image segmentation, which is highly relevant to the ICLR audience.

<Weakness>

•	The novelty of the proposed algorithm is okay. But it is difficult to justify its practical values given experiments in the manuscript. The effectiveness and practical values of the proposed algorithm is unconvincing. Only a single 2D backbone neural network is studied in the experiments. And the results of the proposed algorithm are not compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms on the same datasets or public leaderboards.

•	The tasks in the experiment are relatively easy segmentation tasks of 3D medical images. It would be more practical to apply the proposed algorithm on challenge datasets such as multi-class segmentation or tumor segmentation.

•	Discussion or ablation studies are not sufficient (see below).

<Comments>

1.	What is the additional training cost when applying the proposed algorithm? What is the training efficiency for each algorithm in Table 1?

2.	It would be better to visualize the dynamic weight map in order to further understand the effect of the proposed algorithm.

3.	How many iterations of three-level optimization are required during model training? How to determine when to stop the optimization process?

4.	Is it necessary to have both step 1 and step 3 in the algorithm? They serve the same purpose to optimize segmentation model weights. And the weight maps in step 3 of the first iteration should be the same as ones in step 1 of the second iteration.

5.	Would using a different random seed in model training give similar results?

6.	The 2D segmentation model is used for 3D medical image segmentation. Why not directly use the 3D segmentation models for the tasks?

7.	Both datasets (of binary segmentation) in experiments are relatively easy. It would be more practical to apply the proposed algorithm on challenge datasets such as multi-class segmentation or tumor segmentation.

8.	It is necessary to benchmark the proposed algorithm with more than one backbone networks (e.g., various versions of U-Net models).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The manuscript is of moderate quality, with good clarity and good novelties.
content.summary_of_the_review: My main concern about the manuscript is the practical values of the work. Only a single 2D backbone neural network is used in the experiments. And the tasks in the experiment are relatively easy segmentation tasks of 3D medical images.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper exploits the potential of imperfect supervision for medical image segmentation. Meta-learning bootstrapping, averaging predictions of augmented views of input images, and mean teacher techniques are employed to improve the performance. Through the experiments, the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in semi-supervision and noisy supervision settings.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1) The paper presents the first unified meta-learning framework for medical image segmentation.
2) The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
3) The proposed method achieves superior performance.

Weaknesses:
1) The novelty of the proposed method is limited. It is just a combination of several existing techniques, i.e., meta-learning bootstrapping, averaging predictions of augmented views of input images, and mean teacher.
2) As a paper working on the medical image, there are no specific designs for medical images. It seems that the proposed method can be applied to the general image segmentation task. The authors should further explain the key difference from the general image segmentation task. The few-shot or noisy label setting is not specific to the medical image segmentation. These problems also exist in general image segmentation tasks.
3) Some key details are missing. In Section 3.2, the input is augmented to different views. The authors should clarify what augmentations are used.

One typo is found in Sec 4.5:
It should be "5) MLB + PLE + mean teacher" rather than "4) xxx"

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors presented a meta-learning-based framework, MLB-Seg, for exploiting semi- and noisy- supervision in medical image segmentation. MLB-Seg could learn to dynamically assign pixel weight maps to imperfect labels as well as proportional pseudo-labels and determine this weight in a meta-process. In addition, the authors proposed a consistency-based Pseudo Label Enhancement (PLE) scheme, which uses a mean teacher model to address the instability of weights during the meta-learning process. This paper had well-researched literature and demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method through extensive experiments on the public LA and PROMISE12 benchmarks, with new state of the arts.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

1. Apply meta-learning to semi- and noisy- supervision for medical image segmentation. 
2. Extensive results showed new state of the arts on two public benchmarks. 
3. Very well written, easy to follow. 

Weakness:
1.	No introduction to meta-learning. Also luck of the details of settings of meta-learning, For example, how the Tasks in meta-learning were formed, how the support set and query set were divided, etc.
2.	In Related Work, just describing what other papers is not enough. Comparisons and contrasts need to be added.
3.	Motivation of applying meta-learning to medical image segmentation is not well described. 
4.	The "n" in "Unet" in the bottom of Table 1 should be uppercase "N".
5.	The description for evaluation metrics was missing, such as JI (%), HD (voxel), and ASD (voxel).
6.	If the space allows, it is advisable for the authors to show several segmentation results for comparison.
7.	Only Dice was shown in Table 1, but Dice and ASD were shown in Table 4. Could the authors give reasons for these two choices?
8. Is it possible to provide some statistical tests (p values) for the results shown in those Tables?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity, Quality, Novelty and Reproducibility are acceptable.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposed meta-learning to improve medical image segmentation. It has been evaluated on two public datasets and achieved good results. Presentation of the paper is good, easy to follow. Novelty is also somehow justified.

content.title: Meta-Learning for Bootstrapping Medical Image Segmentation from Imperfect Supervision
content.abstract: Medical imaging has witnessed remarkable progress but usually requires a large amount of high-quality annotated data which is time-consuming and costly to obtain. To alleviate the annotation burden, learning from imperfect supervision (scarce or noisy annotations) has received much attention recently. In this paper, we present Meta-Learning for Bootstrapping Medical Image Segmentation (MLB-Seg), a unified meta-learning framework to sufficiently exploit the potential of imperfect supervision for medical image segmentation. In the face of noisy labeled data and unlabeled data, we first learn a segmentation model from a small clean set to generate initial labels for the unlabeled data and then gradually leverage the learner’s own predictions (i.e., the online pseudo labels) to bootstrap itself up via meta-learning. Specifically, MLB-Seg learns to dynamically assign per-pixel weight maps to both the imperfect labels (including both the generated labels and the noisy labels), as well as the pseudo labels commensurately to facilitate the bootstrapping procedure, where the weights are determined in a meta-process. To further improve the quality of the pseudo labels, we apply a consistency-based Pseudo Label Enhancement (PLE) scheme by ensembling predictions from various augmented versions of the same input. Noticing that the weight maps from these augmented variants can be extremely noisy from the meta-update, mean teacher is introduced into PLE to stabilize the weight map generation from the student (target) meta-learning model. Extensive experimental results on the public atrial and prostate segmentation datasets demonstrate that our method 1) achieves the state-of-the-art result under both semi- and noisy- supervision; 2) is robust against various imperfect supervisions. Code is publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MLB-Seg-C80E.
